transcript:
Header: 2026-06-26 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Nimbus CTO), Maya Gonzalez (Nimbus ML Eng), Evan Brooks (Nimbus DevOps)

Auto-summary: quick recap at top - Redwood shows p50~120ms vs baseline 200ms, p95 ~250ms vs baseline 350ms after applying int8 quant + batching. Still some region variance; eu-west needs re-run.

Topics: Benchmark dataset, latency/throughput numbers, config (quantization, batching, KV cache), infra (VPC, Dedicated vs Hosted), security (SOC2, KMS), next steps and owners.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, two quick goals for today - walk through the benchmark sheet and call out where Redwood beats the baseline and where we still need followups. Liam and I will lead the perf bits.
[00:12] Raj: cool, thanks Sofia. quick note we have Maya and Evan on; Maya will be the lead for model evaluation, Evan on infra. timeline still end of Q3 for pilot decision.
[00:24] Liam: awesome, i'll share my screen with the perf dashboard in a sec. quick context - we ran the same prompt set you provided (conversational + 2k token doc summarization) against Redwood hosted instance and your CloudModelX endpoints with equivalent model family. runs used concurrency sweep 1-8, token lengths 50-1200.
[00:45] Maya: just to confirm, the baseline runs were from your team or ours? i noticed some discrepancies between the baseline logs we had and the sheet.
[00:54] Sofia: good call — baseline logs came from Nimbus's CloudModelX exports that Evan uploaded; we re-run them through our analyzer but kept raw logs intact. we'll send the full CSV.
[01:05] Liam: ok jumping into numbers — overall summary: Redwood p50 latency 120ms, p90 180ms, p95 250ms on host-g4-like instance with int8 quant + batching. CloudModelX p50 200ms, p95 350ms. throughput at steady-state (tokens/sec per GPU): Redwood ~650 t/s, baseline ~420 t/s for the same prompt mix.
[01:35] Raj: those are big deltas, are those numbers for single-request latency or end-to-end with network hops?
[01:42] Liam: these are server-side latencies (time from request entering inference runtime to final token emit) — we stripped client network time. for end-to-end, add region RTT ~30-50ms depending on location.
[01:55] Evan: interesting. in our internal tests we saw more variance in eu-west, sometimes p95 jumps to 450ms. what's the cause? different hardware or batch sizing?
[02:05] Liam: yeah great question. eu-west runs used smaller batch sizes due to lower concurrency in that region during the test; also kernel selection for that particular GPU cluster had suboptimal scheduling causing higher KV cache miss rates — we annotated runs where KV cash (sic) warmed vs cold. once warmed, p95 dropped ~80ms.
[02:25] Maya: when you say int8 quant, is that post-training quant or dynamic quantization? how much quality degradation did you observe?
[02:34] Liam: int8 static quant via our quant recipe for that model; we ran the eval set you provided — aggregate accuracy drop ~0.6% on your ROUGE-style metrics, with some edge-case hallucinations but within your acceptance threshold per earlier convo. we can share the eval diff sheet.
[02:50] Raj: ok sounds reasonable if cost savings are big enough. what's the cost delta?
[02:55] Sofia: rough numbers from the POC: Redwood unit cost per 1M tokens (after batching+quant) ~ $7.2 vs baseline ~ $12.5. that is model + infra amortized; exact pricing for Dedicated will differ with reserved capacity.
[03:12] Evan: those are promising. i noticed spikes in one of the Redwood runs around hour 3 — any autoscaling or preemption there?
[03:20] Liam: that was during a concurrent kernel compaction step after deploy. we had a background compaction job that bumped latency; we've since disabled compaction during steady-state and will re-run long tail tests.
[03:34] Maya: can you walk through the config you used? batch size, max tokens, KV cache policy?
[03:40] Liam: sure — primary run: batch window 20ms, max batch 16, prefix KV caching enabled with LRU eviction, kv warm threshold 8 requests, sequence-length caps at 2k tokens for the doc-summarization flow. quantization int8 static, flash attention kernels where supported. i'll paste the exact command and config after the call.
[03:58] Raj: how reproducible are results? i.e., if we take your config and run in our eu-west region with same instance types, would we get parity?
[04:06] Liam: mostly yes, small differences expected due to GPU driver versions or NVLINK topology. we recommend using our dedicated pools for parity, but host offers identical runtime stacks.
[04:18] Raj: question on security — our security team needs SOC2 Type II docs, SAML SSO, KMS/HSM integration, and audit log retention at least 1 year. can you support that in Hosted?
[04:30] Sofia: yes — for Hosted we have SOC2 artifacts and support SAML + RBAC; KMS integration is available for Dedicated/Private and we offer audit logs export. we'll share the SOC2 pack and a pointer to our compliance page.
[04:40] Evan: we'd likely need VPC peering or private connectivity; do you support Private with customer-managed networking?
[04:46] Sofia: absolutely — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options, customer-managed control plane, and HSM/KMS. for the POC we can spin up a VPC-connected Dedicated pool for the capacity test.
[04:58] Maya: back to perf — did you test the model variants? we have a smaller variant that our baseline uses sometimes; curious about tradeoffs.
[05:06] Liam: yes we tested both base and trimmed variants; smaller variant 30% lower cost but p95 latency improves only modestly because you hit scheduling overheads and network. quantization yields more cost reduction for the larger model.
[05:20] Raj: any concerns about hallucination/regression when quantizing? we need to lock quality thresholds before moving to prod.
[05:27] Liam: agreed — we run eval suites and A/B compare outputs at multiple prompt sets and will flag regressions >1% absolute on your key metrics. also we can do canary rollouts per-route.
[05:38] Evan: on the infra run you mentioned 650 t/s — what's the concurrency footprint for that?
[05:44] Liam: that's at concurrency 6 with batching window of 20ms; if you push concurrency to 12 you get higher aggregate throughput but p95 starts to increase because of tail effects; that's where our autoscaling and prioritized routing helps.
[06:00] Maya: are there memory pressure issues with long sequences? some of our workloads hit 4k tokens occasionally.
[06:06] Liam: at 4k tokens memory goes up nonlinearly; we recommend segmented generation or KV offload. for Dedicated we can allocate larger GPUs or enable kv disk offload. we'll run a 4k token test as a follow-up.
[06:18] Raj: okay wanted to call out cost vs latency tradeoff — we are most sensitive to p95 but need to keep cost reasonable. your numbers look promising but want to see stable eu-west numbers and the security docs.
[06:30] Sofia: understood — next steps are the items we listed. also, based on these results we can propose a short Dedicated pilot (2-4 weeks) with reserved nodes to show production parity.
[06:44] Evan: do you have a recommended pilot sizing? we need guidance to budget.
[06:48] Liam: for your current traffic profiles, we'd recommend 4 reserved GPUs in eu-west with autoscale headroom for burst; that'll keep p95 under 300ms. we'll provide cost estimate in the sheet.
[07:02] Raj: anything else on compliance or procurement? we may need a data processing addendum and subprocessor list.
[07:08] Sofia: we'll attach DPA and subprocessor list in the followup email.
[07:14] Maya: quick nit — in the spreadsheet there's a row labelled "Redwood Dediated" — i'm assuming that's Dedicated? also saw "KV cash" as noted earlier. just wanted to flag small typos in the sheet.
[07:24] Sofia: thanks — we're aware of auto-transcription typos, we'll clean and re-upload. the raw logs will be unmodified.
[07:30] Liam: i'll also call out three runs that show outliers — hours 2-4 in eu-west, the compaction event, and a misconfigured affinity on one node. once we re-run with compaction disabled we expect p95 to converge closer to our host averages.
[07:46] Evan: timeline — we can run the eu-west re-run starting Monday and report by Thursday.
[07:52] Raj: sounds good. last question: in case we go Dedicated, how long to provision nodes?
[07:57] Sofia: for reserved capacity it's about 5-7 business days after PO in typical cases; for quick validation we can spin a short-lived Dedicated pool in 24-48 hours for testing.
[08:08] Maya: ok thanks everyone.
[08:10] Sofia: quick recap / action items — Liam will send config and annotated runs, Sofia will send benchmark CSV, SOC2 and DPA, Evan will run eu-west 24h test. we'll meet again same time next week to review re-run. thanks all.
[08:24] Raj: thanks, bye.

End of transcript. Some speech artifacts: filler words, small mis-transcriptions, and occasional speaker label noise.

References shared: benchmark_spreadsheet.csv (link in chat), SOC2_pack.pdf (link in chat), DPA_template.docx (link in chat).
